Which policies are the claims of ‹claima.plan:
Path: claimant <- FILED_BY - claim - UNDER_POLICY -> policy. The hops run in different directions: FILED_BY goes in (claim -> claimant), UNDER_POLICY goes out (claim -> policy). The rule says to refuse when the hops run in different directions and the relationship type leading the path already joins the anchor to entities of the target type. Here the leading relationship, FILED_BY, joins the claimant to claims, not to policies, so the target type (policy) is not reached by the first hop. The refusal condition does not apply, but one direction applies to all hops. With direction "both", the two hops would work: the first hop from the claimant reaches claims via FILED_BY (in), the second hop reaches policies via UNDER_POLICY (out). With both, the second hop could also go back to the claimant through FILED_BY, but that returns only claimants, not policies. Using via with both relationship types and direction both gives policies.

```json
{"kind":"plan","templateId":"linked-entities","templateVersion":1,"params":{"ref":{"entityType":"claimant","stableId":"‹claimant#1›"},"targetType":"policy","via":["FILED_BY","UNDER_POLICY"],"direction":"both","maxHops":2},"rationale":"Two-hop path from the claimant through claims to policies, using FILED_BY and UNDER_POLICY in both directions."}
```
